findings.title: Cleanup job interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without explanation
findings.body: The background cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This affects the entire `clean()` routine, which runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history), not just the annotation cleanup this PR is about. Running every cleanup job 10x more frequently is a significant behavioral/performance change that is not mentioned in the PR description, is unrelated to the stated goal of avoiding MySQL deadlocks (and could actually increase contention since jobs now run far more often), and has no corresponding test coverage or justification. This looks like it may be a leftover debugging change that should be reverted or explicitly justified before merge.

findings.title: Error-level logging used for normal/successful cleanup batches, including full ID lists
findings.body: In CleanAnnotations (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (lines 576, 579), `r.log.Error(...)` is called on every batch iteration even when there is no error. The `err`/`y` values logged at line 534/554/576 are guaranteed nil at that point because the function already returned early on error, so these statements always report a bogus 'error' for a success case. Since these calls run on every batch of every cleanup cycle (now potentially every minute, with batch sizes that can be in the tens of thousands as exercised by the new test), this will flood error-level logs/alerting systems with non-error noise and also logs the entire fetched ID slice (up to the configured batch size) on every iteration, adding unnecessary log volume/overhead. These should be at Debug/Info level and should not include an always-nil error field.
